key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell designs and pinpoint the layer properties that most strongly drive efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical design rules for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL materials, including lead-free double perovskites, to accelerate high-efficiency photovoltaic device optimization.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used Leave-One-Group-Out validation and SHAP to assess ranking performance and feature importance.
evidence_signal: The model showed reliable ranking via Spearman correlation in cross-validation, and full SCAPS-1D verification identified devices such as FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE and FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.62% PCE.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the simulation fidelity and coverage of the training subset, so real-device performance may differ due to fabrication defects, interface quality, and materials stability.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
